name: Real-World Class-Level Code Generation Benchmark
description: Large language models (LLMs) have demonstrated strong performance on function-level code generation benchmarks, yet real-world software development increasingly demands class-level implementations that integrate multiple methods, attributes, and dependencies within authentic project contexts. This gap between benchmark performance and practical utility raises critical questions about LLMs' readiness for production code assistance, particularly regarding their ability to generalize across familiar and novel codebases. We introduce a benchmark derived from real-world open-source repositories, comprising classes divided into seen and unseen partitions to evaluate generalization under practical conditions. reputation: A recent research benchmark with limited community adoption so far, mainly used in the paper introducing it.
notes: Likely a relatively new and small benchmark; class-level generation is harder than function-level code generation and may be sensitive to repository overlap and retrieval setup.
